sources.title: Meta and Microsoft Introduce the Next Generation of Llama
sources.evidence: Dated July 18, 2023; announces availability that day and distribution of model weights and starting code for pretrained and conversationally fine-tuned models.

sources.title: Llama-2-7b-hf official model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Identifies this exact repository as the 7B pretrained model converted to Transformers format; its model-details table explicitly gives 7B parameters, 4k context and no GQA. Names Meta and text-only inputs/outputs. Download access requires license acceptance. No separate active count appears in the card.

sources.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Table 1 explicitly gives Llama 2 7B, 4k trained context and no GQA, distinct from the original Llama 1 7B row. Section 2.2 describes Transformer, RMSNorm, SwiGLU and RoPE. Section 5.1 tool-use experiment concerns Llama 2-Chat. The Meta report does not define an active-parameter count.

sources.title: Llama 2 Community License Agreement
sources.evidence: Names the custom Llama 2 Community License Agreement and July 18, 2023 version release date; licenses weights and code, with acceptable-use obligations and additional commercial terms.

sources.title: Original Llama 2 inference repository README
sources.evidence: Release includes pretrained/fine-tuned weights; documents license-gated downloads, maximum 4096 sequence length, and natural-continuation inference for pretrained models, which are not fine-tuned for chat or Q&A.

sources.title: Llama 2 reference Transformer implementation
sources.evidence: Transformer uses causal attention and unconditional SwiGLU feed-forward layers, with no expert router. Attention defaults KV heads to query heads. Embeddings and output projection are separate. ModelArgs max_seq_len default is a runtime setting, not training evidence.

sources.title: Llama 2 reference generation implementation
sources.evidence: Loads checkpoint params, explicitly supplies runtime max_seq_len, and exposes token/text completion. No dedicated thinking channel or structured function-call interface is defined.

sources.title: Original Llama 2 model card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Lists Meta, nominal 7B pretrained/fine-tuned variants, text-only inputs/outputs, autoregressive Transformer and 4k/no-GQA row for 7B; distinguishes tuned variants and calls the license custom commercial. Its parameter table does not separately report active parameters.

sources.title: Exact official checkpoint configuration (access restricted)
sources.evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 401 requiring permission and authentication. No configuration content or tensor headers were obtained; no gate bypass or weight download was attempted.

sources.title: Mixtral of Experts — Table 2 active-parameter comparison
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Table 2 explicitly labels the column Active Params and assigns 7B to the exact LLaMA 2 7B comparison row. Section 3 evaluates base models; instruction fine-tuning is handled separately in Section 4. This is Mistral's published nominal active-count convention for Meta's model, not a direct Meta active-count disclosure or an exact per-token tensor inventory.

sources.title: JetMoE original project page — benchmark active-parameter table
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The original benchmark table explicitly gives LLaMA2-7B Active Params 7B and Training Tokens 2T. Its separate LLaMA-13B row uses 1T, and chat models appear in a separate MT-Bench table, establishing the Llama 2 base identity. Corroborates Mistral's whole-billion nominal active-count convention.

sources.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models — Figure 7
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and visually inspected Figure 7 on PDF page 18. The horizontal axis is Number of Activated Parameters (Billions); the exact LLaMA2 7B point is near 6.7B, with the original LLaMA 7B separately labeled. This approximate plotted value is compatible with the coarser nominal 7B in Mistral's and JetMoE's explicit tables; the chart supplies neither an exact scalar count nor a component breakdown.

name.note: Official 7B pretrained/base variant; the separate Llama-2-7b-chat checkpoint is outside this record.

developer.note: Both official cards identify Meta as model developer; Microsoft is a distribution partner.

family.note: Catalog slug normalizes the explicitly named Llama 2 family.

release_date.note: Original public availability date is explicit in the launch announcement and license; independent of repository creation or later Transformers updates.

open_weights.note: Meta released downloadable pretrained weights subject to access approval and its custom license. This does not assert an unrestricted or OSI-approved license.

license.note: Exact custom license, with use restrictions and additional commercial terms; not Apache/MIT.

parameters_b.note: Freshly rechecked Meta's exact pretrained model card, original model card and technical-report Table 1. Retains the explicitly published nominal 7B total, in billions, without claiming exactly 7,000,000,000 learned scalars. This is the Llama 2 base checkpoint, not the original LLaMA 7B or Llama 2-Chat.

active_parameters_b.note: Mistral's Mixtral Table 2 explicitly assigns Active Params 7B to LLaMA 2 7B; JetMoE's original base-model comparison independently lists 7B. Adopt their whole-billion nominal active-count convention, attributed to those research teams rather than to Meta. DeepSeekMoE Figure 7 places the separately identified LLaMA2 7B point at approximately 6.7B, compatible at the selected precision. No exact per-token scalar count or component scope is inferred, and the value is not obtained merely by equating dense total and active counts.

architecture.note: Dense causal Transformer: standard attention and unconditional SwiGLU blocks, with RMSNorm/RoPE and no expert routing. The 7B row explicitly excludes GQA; it uses ordinary multi-head attention, unlike larger GQA variants.

context_window.note: Original trained context is 4k, made exact as 4096 in Meta's inference README. Runtime cache limits/defaults are configurable and do not replace this limit; no later context-extension fine-tune is included.

modalities.note: Both official model cards explicitly restrict input/output modalities to text.

reasoning.note: No dedicated native thinking mode is documented for the pretrained base. Commonsense/math benchmark results or prompted chain-of-thought text do not establish a separate reasoning-mode capability; no absolute inability is inferred.

tool_call.note: No native structured tool-call protocol is documented for this base checkpoint. Paper Section 5.1 describes Llama 2-Chat tool-use experiments, which cannot be transferred to 7B base; external wrappers also do not establish native support.

description.note: Accurate concise description of the base pretrained release; does not claim chat alignment, tools or multimodality.

patch.notes: 7B is Meta's nominal total size. Nominal active 7B follows Mistral's and JetMoE's explicit comparison tables; DeepSeek plots approximately 6.7B. These research-team conventions do not establish an exact per-token count or a direct Meta active-count disclosure. This dense pretrained text model uses multi-head attention, 4096-token context and the custom Llama 2 Community License. Native thinking/tool-call support is not separately documented.

conflicts: The paper introduction broadly mentions adopting GQA, but Table 1 limits it to larger variants; the exact 7B row is no-GQA.

Reference ModelArgs defaults max_seq_len to 2048, while the README explicitly supports 4096 and generation builds ModelArgs with a supplied max_seq_len. The default is an allocation/inference choice, not the trained context.

Model-card family prose includes Chat fine-tuning and benchmarks. Repository identity explicitly identifies this checkpoint as pretrained; Chat-specific tool emergence is not evidence of base-model native tool calls.
The public exact model card was accessible, but the exact config download returned 401. Third-party config mirrors surfaced in search were not used as first-party verification.

Active-count precision differs across original comparisons: Mistral Table 2 and JetMoE explicitly give nominal 7B, while DeepSeekMoE Figure 7 plots LLaMA2 7B near 6.7B. Retain the explicit whole-billion table convention; these values are compatible at that precision. Neither the approximate plot nor the nominal tables establish an exact per-token tensor inventory, and none is a direct Meta active-count disclosure.
summary: Fresh parameter re-audit on October 27, 2026 retains Meta's verified nominal 7B total and resolves active parameters from null/undisclosed to verified nominal 7B using Mistral Table 2 and JetMoE's original comparison table. DeepSeekMoE Figure 7 independently supplies an approximately 6.7B plotted convention, compatible with the selected whole-billion precision. Reopened Meta's exact base card, original model card and technical report; searched exact active/activated-parameter terms and later original comparisons. No separate Meta active-count disclosure or exact scalar count was established. The other twelve assessments are unchanged, including native thinking/tool calling remaining null/undisclosed.
